points.description: Gives the best-case operation count as N (the number of elements / length of the array), i.e. linear in N. Accept N-1, 'N comparisons/operations', 'proportional to array length', or O(N)/linear time as equivalent.
Identifies the best-case input as an array that is already sorted (in order). Accept 'sorted array', 'already sorted', or 'elements in ascending order'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer says nearly/mostly sorted but not fully sorted.

levels.says: Says the array is nearly/mostly sorted, or otherwise close to sorted, but not fully sorted.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the linear/N operation count and the already-sorted input. Award the operation-count point for N, N-1, or an equivalent linear/O(N) statement; award the scenario point for an already sorted array. Do not award the scenario point for reverse-sorted, random, or unsorted input; a nearly sorted answer earns only half of that point.
